checks: The equivalent Minkowski condition follows by grouping the coefficients of any convex combination in the lifted hull by base. Completeness is needed only to identify the lifted hull's mixed lattice slice and the reduced positive-site set with the full lattice intersections.

For z in the relative interior of its minimal face F, the displacement away from the mean of all sites of P in F can be taken arbitrarily small. Mixing that displacement back with the mean gives positive coefficients at all those sites, including sites that are not vertices. One positive fiber then contributes a positively scaled full-dimensional body after choosing one point in every other contributing fiber. This works for F a singleton and when F equals conv(P).

If every fiber on F is null, positive total mass makes F proper, so its affine exposer gives an actual nontrivial vertical closed cap through the point with zero mass. If some fiber on F is positive, the affine hull of its lifted face hull contains every continuous direction and projects onto aff(F), so it is aff(F) times R^d. Compatibility gives the exact fiber at z. A boundary point in that fiber is on the relative boundary of the lifted face hull. A nonconstant supporting margin there cannot be a pure base margin because z is relatively interior in F. Extend the margin to the ambient space and add a finite multiple of the exposer. Compactness and finitely many strict off-face gaps exclude all off-face fibers, and the nonzero continuous normal makes every face trace null.

At an interior point, restricting any containing ambient halfspace to the anchored fiber gives the whole ball or at least half the ball. Positive total mass ensures at least one such point. For existence of the asserted maximum, at a fixed ambient normal a through-point cap mass is upper semicontinuous in the point by closedness and reverse Fatou. The infimum over normals remains upper semicontinuous on the compact lifted set. Thus deletion of exclusively zero-depth points preserves the positive attained maximum.

For w in P intersect conv(P_+), at least one positive-volume contributor has positive coefficient and the entire Minkowski combination lies in K_w. Thus w is retained, even if its base is not a vertex. Inclusion of the smaller lifted hull in the original and inclusion of the original retained lifts in the smaller hull give exactly the same retained fibers. Lattice completeness passes to P_+ by the inclusion conv(P_+) subset conv(P).

overlap.comparison: The planar central-fiber proof with n=1 and d=2 already gives zero depth at the boundary and positive depth in the interior of the chosen positive-area fiber. It uses a supporting affine envelope over heights. It does not supply the all-base minimal-face or exact null-fiber deletion claims in general dimension.

The null singleton fibers of its two explicit parity constructions have zero actual ambient depth. Its result uses their construction-specific geometry and does not characterize all fiber boundaries or prove completeness and measure preservation after support reduction.

readability: An optional sentence can justify attainment of the maximum using upper semicontinuity and compactness. This follows directly from the closed-halfspace definition and does not require another same-wave result.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: Compatibility at every represented base propagates positive volume within the relevant minimal face. A relative supporting cap gives zero depth at every fiber boundary and a centered ball gives positive depth at every interior point. Deletion of null fibers leaves the exact measure and its maximal depth intact.
